deck: Industrial design and product development engineer. Objects that can be manufactured, interfaces that get used and the code that ties them together, from idea to part.
coverCaption: SEAT Ateca side mirror redesign, assembly view. Scroll to take it apart.

featured.deck: A mirror that folds itself before it hits something, and keeps the driver seeing when it does.
featured.approach: Ultrasonic folding, camera view on the central screen, blind-spot radar and a dynamic LED indicator, validated against ECE R46 and in SolidWorks Simulation.
featured.role: Regulatory analysis, circuit redesign, material specs, renders

featured.deck: A plant pot that waters itself on indoor light, so the plant survives the holidays.
featured.approach: Organic photovoltaic film, a positive-displacement pump dosing 250 ml, a lift-out rPET tank and a recycled PP body with no glue or paint.
featured.role: Led the development phase and CAD, renders

featured.deck: A simpler, cheaper bikepacking rack with a hanger to dry clothes on the move.
featured.approach: Material teardown of the original rack, a single bent aluminium frame and a hanger that lifts 90° and turns 180° out of the wind.
featured.role: Market and use analysis, ideation, specs, manufacturing

featured.deck: A home on a windy hill above Donostia that makes its own energy and reuses its rain.
featured.approach: Hybrid PV-thermal panels, a small wind turbine, a heat pump, rainwater harvesting and recycled cellulose insulation.

featured.deck: Taking a premium air vent apart to find where its footprint hides, then cutting it.
featured.approach: Cradle-to-grave LCA with the IHOBE calculator, hotspot analysis and nine redesign concepts. The final concept cuts the carbon footprint by about 85 %.

procedure.title: From sketch to part.
procedure.intro: Five phases that repeat in every project, whether it is an injected housing, a robot or an app.

steps.label: Phase 1
steps.title: Research
steps.text: Users, context, regulations and competitors. Understand the problem before drawing anything.

steps.label: Phase 2
steps.title: Conceptualise
steps.text: Sketches, quick mock-ups and use scenarios. Many cheap ideas to pick a good one.

steps.label: Phase 3
steps.title: Model and validate
steps.text: CAD, calculation, manufacturability and rendering, to decide with data and with images.

steps.label: Phase 4
steps.title: Prototype
steps.text: 3D printing, electronics and clickable interfaces. Test, break and fix.

steps.label: Phase 5
steps.title: Implement
steps.text: Drawings and documentation for production, automation or code ready to ship.
